evidence_quotes.two_concerns_question: we talked to a lot of customers about concerns on their move like, damages to their items or movers not showing up or any of this a concern of yours. (asked after email and name collection, during probing phase)
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: Customer said 'Not really' to concerns; no follow-up probing occurred — n/a because no concern was raised
evidence_quotes.value_days: Joanna mentioned Monday is 'one of our lowest hourly rate for the week, which is $102 per hour per mover' but never offered an alternative cheaper day, never framed as a total dollar saving, and never asked about date flexibility
evidence_quotes.rate_lock_then_ask: Joanna asked 'would you like our help for this move on November 9th?' with no rate lock or no-deposit language preceding it; customer deferred ('I can think about it and get back to you') and rep pivoted to email follow-up rather than anchoring commitment

top_strength: Joanna gathered comprehensive logistics details efficiently—moving only bedroom items, furniture list, destination floor/stairs, parking proximity, packing preferences—and delivered a specific anchored range ($585–$789, 2.5–3.5 hours) tailored to the third-floor apartment context.
coaching_note: Step 6 was skipped entirely (no final concerns check); also step 5 never addressed value days or prep framing, and step 7's ask came without rate lock or no-deposit language, leaving the customer with no urgency anchor before they deferred to think it over.
